extracted.intended_audience: Governor‑General and Council / Select Committee / East India Company officials
extracted.subtask_description: Practices and policy criteria for administering assigned districts in the Carnatic: realizing revenues, letting leases, retrenching expenses, protecting renters, and maintaining local infrastructure and customs during wartime and transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entire alteration in the mode of realizing the revenues
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend an entire change of system to recover revenues thought irrecoverably lost under previous management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors proposed a considerable and immediate reduction of expenses and a total change of the principal aumildars employed under the Nabob, arguing that only a complete change could restore revenue collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letting districts by public advertisement in the Company's name
rubrics_metrics.description: Advertise districts to be farmed out by public advertisement issued in the Company's name and circulated through every province.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To encourage bidders, advertise for the whole period of the Nabob's assignment and promise the security of the Company's protection to renters; the number and terms of proposals are used as evidence of the plan's success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of renters under the Company's sole authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Appoint renters under Company authority when Nabob's servants obstruct information and accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Company judged it expedient to let districts to renters under its sole authority because Nabob's servants evaded orders and withheld accounts; appointing renters was viewed as the only prospect for successful collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerable retrenchment in all articles of expense
rubrics_metrics.description: Retrench considerably in district expenses; prefer risking too much retrenchment over too little.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended reductions were based on inquiries showing extravagant charges; the committee chose to incur the hazard of retrenching too much because it is easier later to add necessary allowances than to diminish inflated ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discriminate military charges from civil revenue-collection charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate charges for troops (defence) from those for sibbendy, servants, cultivation and revenue collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful discrimination was necessary to avoid blending legitimate public charities and customs with items that had been used to conceal misappropriation; this improves transparency and prevents fraud and oppression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve established customs, privileges and public charities where proper
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow necessary established customs, ancient privileges, and public charities that should be continued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While retrenching expenses, attention must be paid to customs and privileges that are proper to continue; these had previously been rated higher and blended into vague expense categories, allowing concealment of revenues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enroll Nabob's sepoys into Company service or discharge them
rubrics_metrics.description: Receive into Company's service those of the Nabob's sepoys who will enlist, and discharge the rest, striking related charges out of accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This relieves the country's burden and helps fix Company authority for revenue collection; any future additions to Company forces for assigned countries should be deducted from present savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for future additions to military establishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Deduct the expense of any post-war additions to the Company's military establishment (for assigned countries) from present account of savings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If present reduction of Nabob's artillery makes post-war additions expedient, their expense must be charged against current savings to avoid overstating financial benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect renters' lease rights unless they breach covenants
rubrics_metrics.description: Renters who entered covenants under public advertisement are to be maintained in their leases; leases cannot be legally torn away absent the renters' breach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renters applied in reliance on Company's joint authority with the Nabob and entered mutual covenants; stripping them of leases would be arbitrary and oppressive, and the Company must consider effects on innocent third parties before surrendering the assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide protection to calm apprehensions of native bidders
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer the Company's protection to calm fears (e.g., of Nabob vengeance) so natives will bid or accept renterships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example cited of a Bramin imprisoned on rumor — government promise of protection was necessary to reassure the people and induce participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer local managers knowledgeable of customs and manners
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid appointing strangers unfamiliar with local customs to manage districts; prefer persons from the country who understand manners and customs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strangers oppressed inhabitants and disturbed cultivation, causing farmers to fail; local managers would better preserve order and collection performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be moderate in demands on native rulers; avoid excessive deposits/rents
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not demand money (rents/deposits) beyond a country's capacity to pay; be moderate and adapt demands to local circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Witness testimony that Rajah of Tanjore could not pay excessive deposit-money and that over-demanding led to borrowing at exorbitant interest and decline of cultivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require statements of accounts to assess ability to pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Request the ruler to produce statements of accounts, disbursements, debts, and payments to ascertain the country's ability to pay increased demands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No evidence that such statements were required historically; the committee implies this is a necessary step for fiscal prudence before escalating demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance seed and maintain irrigation to sustain cultivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the custom (and necessity) that the proprietor advances seed to cultivators and funds maintenance of mounds and watercourses; extortion that removes such advances harms cultivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide seed and maintain waterworks leads to uncultivated districts and long-term revenue loss; preserving these payments is an investment in future rents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize repair and protection of major irrigation works (e.g., the Anicut)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep major works like the Anicut in good repair because they are essential to the prosperity and irrigation of whole regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglect increases repair costs and risks general injury to the country; evidence of attempts to prevent repairs should be investigated and punished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid manipulative language/transmission practices in official correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure translations and channels of communication do not allow intermediaries to misrepresent the ruler's intentions (e.g., changing language of correspondence to enable manipulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee criticizes translating correspondence into English and then relaying to the Nabob, which permitted Mr. Benfield to 'relate and read what he pleases' and thus exercise undue ascendency; maintain fidelity and transparency of original-language documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider effects on third parties before altering or surrendering assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Before ordering surrender of the assignment, consider likely effects on third parties (renters) who have not breached engagements and who relied on Company's assurances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compelling aumils to deliver over charges or retaining trusts without protecting renters would create arbitrary despotism; gratitude and humanity require protection of those exposed to vengeance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against concentration of power in local intermediaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid concentrating authority in individuals whose conduct and character suggest they will prosecute projects to the injury of the Company and individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee recommends restraint of the Amir's power and removal of persons like Mr. Benfield from positions where their ascendency could injure public interest; appointments should be scrutinized for conflicts and prior conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use public advertising and transparency to counter secret obstruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ public advertisement and transparent procedures to encourage legitimate proposals and to expose secret attempts to counteract policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The success of public advertisement (number and terms of proposals) was used as evidence that openness encouraged bidders and revealed clandestine opposition to the plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide explicit accounting conventions and unit conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: State conversion rules (e.g., pagodas, rupees, chuckrums) and rounding conventions in fiscal statements to avoid fractions and confusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comparative statement specifies conversions (Madras Pagodas at 10% Batta; Chuckrums at two thirds of a Porto Novo Pagoda; Rupees at 350 per 100 Star Pagodas) and notes rounding to nearest integral numbers for clarity in accounts.
